replays.text:
## Is the Tenergy T320 worth buying?

**Yes, but only if you need a compact power station for light-duty use.** At $225.99, the Tenergy T320 is a reasonable buy for camping, charging electronics, and short-term emergency backup. However, it's not a particularly good value if you need higher power output or faster recharging.

<AsyncImage query="Tenergy T320 300Wh portable power station black LCD display front two AC outlets" aspectRatio="5:4"/>

### What I like about it

| Feature | Assessment |
|---|---|
| 300Wh LiFePO4 battery | Good chemistry and longevity |
| 200W continuous / 400W surge | Adequate for small electronics |
| 2 pure sine wave AC outlets | Good for sensitive electronics |
| USB-C PD 45W | Useful for phones and laptops |
| 3.7 kg (8.2 lbs) | Reasonably portable |
| 2-year warranty | Good manufacturer coverage |

The LiFePO4 battery is a major plus. Dealectric lists approximately 2,000 cycles, while Walmart's listing claims 3,500+ cycles. I'd treat the cycle-life claims cautiously, but the chemistry itself is a positive.

Sources: [Tenergy official product page](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-t320-portable-power-station-300wh-battery-110v-200w-surge-400w-two-pure-sine-wave-ac-outputs-usb-type-c-pd-45w-solar-ready-mobile-power-for-outdoors-camping-vans-rv-hunting-emergency-backup/) · [Dealectric review](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station) · [Walmart listing](https://business.walmart.com/ip/Tenergy-T320-300-Watthhour-Portable-Power-Station-LiFePO4-Battery-200Watt-Surge-400W/620520170)

### What I don't like

**1. Only 200W continuous output.** This is the biggest limitation. It won't run typical heaters, kettles, coffee makers, hair dryers, or most power tools.

**2. Slow charging.** Approximately 8 hours from AC is quite slow for a 300Wh station.

**3. Limited solar compatibility.** Its 5–24V solar input restricts your panel choices. Many larger portable solar panels have an open-circuit voltage that exceeds this limit. You need to check voltage compatibility carefully.

**4. No expandable battery capacity.** At 300Wh, it's a small power station. Running a device at 100W could theoretically drain it in around 3 hours, before accounting for conversion losses.

Source: [Dealectric — T320 specifications and caveats](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station)
